const keep = bytes.lastIndexOf(0x0a) + 1; // through the last COMPLETE line
      if (keep < bytes.length) {
evidence.reason: The current repair only inspects bytes after the last newline. When the file already ends with a newline, `keep === bytes.length`, so a malformed final content line such as `{"actionId":\n` is never checked or truncated. `record()` then appends a valid record after it; the malformed line is no longer the final line, so `load()` no longer treats it as a droppable truncated tail and throws, stopping dispatch. This is an implementation defect in the existing log-repair behavior; the smallest fix is to locate the last non-blank line as `load()` does and truncate it if it does not parse before appending.
